ticket.title: task(ipc): implement the X05-T2 channel table in keld-ipc — every production consumer derives its id from it, generated TypeScript constants with a drift check, the three hand copies retired
ticket.tier: n/a (program ticket; owns no Electron member)
ticket.current_behavior:
FACT (origin/main 29a4cd70):
- echo = 1 and lifecycle = 3 are defined in keld-ipc; fs = 2 is defined in keld-native.
- The TypeScript app-link transport mirrors 1 and 3, checked by a source-text parity test.
- The macOS renderer bridge carries its own hand copy of echo = 1, with no parity test and no keld-ipc dependency.
- No single table lists the allocated ids.
ticket.what_to_build:
Implement the channel table the approved X05-T2 spec defines.
- One keld-ipc-owned table holding the existing entries (echo, fs, lifecycle), each with name, u16 id, receive-policy class and a keld-guard capability reference or host-internal marker.
- keld-ipc echo/lifecycle, keld-native fs and the macOS renderer bridge derive their ids from the table, the bridge by the mechanism the spec chose.
- The TypeScript transport constants are generated from the table by cold maintainer tooling, following the KEL-98 pattern, and checked in with a drift check; the source-text parity test is retired.
- Table validation rejects duplicate ids and entries without a capability reference or host-internal marker.
Wire bytes and protocol version 2 stay unchanged. This ticket adds no entry beyond the three existing channels: each dependant adds its own entry under the X05-T2 rule when it lands.
ticket.key_interfaces: keld-ipc channel table; generated TypeScript channel constants and drift check; macOS renderer bridge construction; keld-guard capability names by reference.
acceptance_criteria: Every production channel-id use (echo, fs, lifecycle, macOS bridge echo) resolves to a table entry; a test finds zero numeric channel-id literals in production code outside the table
The TypeScript transport's channel constants are generated from the table and checked in; the drift check fails the build when they differ
The table rejects two entries with the same id
Every table entry declares a keld-guard capability name or an explicit host-internal marker
The table contains no per-family id range and no Electron API or family name
Existing kipc golden vectors and the hostile receiver corpus pass unmodified, and the protocol version stays 2
negative_controls: Hand-editing the generated TypeScript channel constant makes the drift check fail
Reintroducing a literal echo id in the macOS renderer bridge makes the no-literal test fail
Adding a second entry with id 2 makes the uniqueness test fail
An entry with neither a capability name nor the host-internal marker makes table validation fail
Inserting a per-family id range entry makes the no-family-name test fail
Renumbering echo from 1 to 4 in the table makes the golden-vector replay fail

Handshake-time channel resolution and HELLO changes; general schema codegen and `keld gen`; per-family reserved ranges (refused); a capability-name registry (keld-guard manifest schema stays the single owner); any el:<channel> grant shape (F04-T3, X04-T1).
